messages.subject: n_eff=1 in RStan 2.5.0 (but not in 2.4.0)
parts:
We're working on a discrete-time multivariate Gaussian state space model, in which we have time series from a number of different sites, with a random intercept for sites. The process model for time t at site i is

y_{i,t} ~ MVN(mu + a_i + A*y_{i,t-1},Sigma)

where mu is a common intercept, a_i is a random intercept, A is a matrix, and Sigma is a covariance matrix. The observation model for the jth observation at the ith site is

z_j ~ MVN(y_j,Eta)

where Eta is a covariance matrix. There are some time points at which some sites aren't observed (I've skipped over the details of how we match up observations with corresponding true states).

In RStan 2.4.0 on 64-bit Ubuntu, everything seemed to work OK (although I'm sure it's not very efficient code). In RStan 2.5.0, if the warmup is long enough, we get n_eff=1 for all parameters (their values remain constant). Maybe we did something wrong that leads to an overflow or underflow, that in turn causes a gradient problem? And somehow we got away with it in 2.4.0?

R script and stan code attached, along with some example data files (ddatasim.txt, tmatch.txt, yrefs.txt, all needed to run the code) and output of sessionInfo() in R.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] n_eff=1 in RStan 2.5.0 (but not in 2.4.0)
parts:
I don't know much about this kind of model, but we have been
tinkering with the multivariate error checking, so that may
be causing problems. But that's probably not the root cause of
the problem.

For both statistical efficiency (high n_eff per iteration)
and computational efficiency (fast iterations), this model
needs to be rewritten with Cholesky factor parameters. The
problem is that we can't literally do that for your model because
we don't (yet) have (inverse) Wishart densities with Cholesky-factor
parameters.

We'd recommend using a correlation matrix parameterization and
an LKJ prior on correlation matrixes. There's a section in the regression
chapter of the 2.5 manual that explains how to code it.

As written, the y[k] where firstyear[k] == 1 will be problematic because
the model doesn't provide the same support as the parameter
declaration for y, which is unconstrained. This will kill any trajectory
explored by the sampler that moves into a region where the density
is 0 (outside min_y and max_y).

If you really need that uniform density with limited support, you
need to declare a different parameter vector with constraint
<lower=min_y,upper=max_y> for the parameters y[k] for which
firstyear[k] == 1. But it'll probably be easier just to put
a normal density such as

normal((max_y - min_y)/2, (max_y - min_y)/4);

For computational efficiency, the best thing to do would be to use
the vector form of all the densities. It'll probably speed up the
code by a factor of 2 to 10 depending on dimensionality. It'd
be a bit tricky with the switch on firstyear[k] == 1 unless you
define two local vectors (or even better a separate parameter vectors)
for the k such that firstyear[k] == 1; this is a separate motivation
to the constraint).

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] n_eff=1 in RStan 2.5.0 (but not in 2.4.0)
parts:
Hi Bob

Thanks for those suggestions. The only one I've implemented so far is changing the uniform density for y[k] (where firstyear[k]==1 is true) to a normal density (mean 0, standard deviation 10). The uniform density is often used for this kind of model, but a normal with a high standard deviation is also fine. That did sound as though it might be the issue, but turns out it didn't make much difference. The others will take a bit more effort. I'm sure they will make the code more efficient, but I also think that it may be changes to multivariate error checking that are the main reason why we get n_eff=1 for all parameters in STAN 2.5, but not 2.4. I've attached representative trace plots for four of the parameters, under both versions. These have the same pseudorandom number seeds, and it looks like everything is behaving the same for about the first 1800 iterations, and then suddenly the STAN 2.5 version stops changing.

Matt
